title: The Cracked Roof
subtitle: Parents refuse to send children back after a classroom ceiling fell
coldOpen: Friday. A classroom ceiling comes down at lunch.
Nobody is hurt. Monday, the yard is empty.
Parents are outside with their own engineer.

briefing.grievance: Parents want proof the building is safe before their children go back, and they want to know why a known crack was painted over in June.
knownFacts: A false ceiling panel fell in Room 4; the structural slab is intact per the first inspection.
A maintenance request about cracks was filed in June and marked “painted”.
Two hundred children have missed two days of classes.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the whole block is condemned and the city is hiding it.
A message says the headteacher ignored three warnings.
briefing.responsibility: You run the schools office and the works department. The children’s safety and the parents’ trust are the same problem.
briefing.objective: Get an independent inspection parents accept, reopen what is safe, and answer the June request honestly.

decisions.title: An empty school
decisions.situation: Two hundred children are home. Parents are at the gate with their own engineer. The headteacher is asking whether to open or close.

options.title: Order a joint inspection today
options.preview: The works engineer and the parents’ engineer check every room together today.
options.authority: Due process: establish the facts before acting on them
options.consequence: Both engineers walk the block. Parents watch from the yard.

options.title: Meet the parents in the yard with the June file
options.preview: You show the June request and the “painted” reply, and say it was wrong.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: The admission is the first thing parents have heard that they believe.

options.title: Threaten fines for non-attendance
options.preview: A notice: children absent from tomorrow will lose their year.
options.authority: Right to education: safety first, coercion never
options.consequence: Frightened parents are threatened instead of answered.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Keep the gates open and see who comes
options.preview: No inspection, no meeting; the yard stays empty.
options.consequence: A third day of classes is lost.

rightsMoments.question: Parents keep children home after a ceiling fell. Can the city force attendance with fines?

options.text: No. The right to education includes a safe school; the duty is to make it safe and show it, not to coerce attendance.
options.feedback: Correct. The state’s obligation runs toward providing safe schooling; coercion does not discharge it.

options.text: Yes. Attendance is compulsory and parents are breaking the law.
options.feedback: Compulsory education obliges the state to provide a safe school before it can demand attendance.

options.text: Yes, once a single official certifies the building.
options.feedback: A certificate without an inspection parents can trust does not make the building safe.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 21A guarantees education, which the state must provide safely; Article 21 protects life. Trust is restored by verifiable inspection, not by penalties.
rightsMoments.why: A joint inspection with the parents’ own engineer did what a threatening notice could not.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)
